title: Interrupt vectors and saved context
text: A PDP-11 interrupt vector contains two words: the new program counter, then the new processor status word at vector address +2. On the PDP-11/70 the service address is in Kernel virtual address space. The old PC and PS are saved on the stack selected by the new status. RTI or RTT restores PC and PS from the stack. A vector is not a single instruction word.
keywords: interrupt interrupts vector vectors rti rtt 1170-vectors
question: Explain Interrupt vectors and saved context.

title: Registers, stacks and processor status
text: R7 is the program counter; R6 is the stack pointer. The PDP-11/70 has two sets of R0–R5 and separate Kernel, Supervisor and User stack pointers. The processor status word selects the register set, current and previous modes and priority, and contains N, Z, V and C condition codes plus the trace bit. This is the /70 organization, not a claim that every PDP-11 has identical registers.
keywords: registers stack pointer status psw r6 r7 1170-registers
question: Explain Registers, stacks and processor status.

title: Autodecrement happens before access
text: For autodecrement addressing, -(Rn), the register is decremented before its contents are used as the operand address. In the handbook examples INC -(R0) decrements R0 by two before incrementing the addressed word; INCB -(R0) decrements R0 by one before incrementing the addressed byte. These R0 examples do not establish SP or PC special cases.
question: Explain Autodecrement happens before access.

title: UNIBUS and memory-mapped devices
text: UNIBUS carries address, data and control signals. Peripheral registers are assigned addresses and can be accessed with the same instruction mechanisms as memory. Transfers are asynchronous and interlocked: the receiving device responds to complete a transfer. Bus mastership can pass from the processor to another device such as a disk controller. This describes hardware organization, not a guest driver or permission to access host devices.

title: V7 ls: listing and ordering
text: The UNIX V7 ls manual says a directory argument lists its contents and no argument lists the current directory. Default ordering is alphabetical. -t sorts by modification time, latest first; -r reverses the chosen ordering. -d lists a directory name rather than its contents. These are V7 options; GNU long options are not established by this source.

title: V7 shell redirection
text: In the V7 shell, < selects a file for standard input. > creates an output file or truncates an existing file to zero length. >> appends to an existing file or creates it if absent. Redirection can change guest files; use a deliberately chosen disposable path. These facts do not establish modern shell extensions or host-shell access.
keywords: v7 shell redirection append truncate v7-redirection
question: Explain V7 shell redirection.

title: V7 ed: entering text
text: In UNIX V7 ed, the a command appends text after the addressed line. Input ends with a line containing just a period. Text is edited in the buffer; consult the w command before expecting changes to be saved to a file. This is a line editor, not vi insert mode, and the example is for V7 ed.

title: VT100 cursor positioning
text: In VT100 ANSI mode, CUP uses ESC [ followed by line and column parameters separated by a semicolon and final H. Defaults are line 1 and column 1. Line numbering depends on origin mode (DECOM). These are terminal protocol bytes; the guest TERM setting must match the selected terminal behavior.

question: Explain VT100 cursor positioning.

title: VT52 compatibility is a distinct mode
text: The VT100 manual distinguishes ANSI mode from VT52-compatible mode. VT52 direct cursor address uses ESC Y followed by row and column characters encoded with an offset of octal 040. ANSI CUP uses numeric parameters instead. A VT100 in VT52-compatible mode does not make the two protocols interchangeable. This source does not qualify a full VT220 implementation.

title: SIMH disk and tape families
text: The SIMH PDP-11 manual distinguishes RK11/RK05 (RK), RL11 with RL01/RL02 (RL), TM11/TU10 (TM), and Massbus TM02/TM03 tape formatters (TU). They are different controller and media families, not interchangeable file suffixes. Simulator device support does not establish that an installed guest has its matching driver. This note is descriptive and supplies no media attachment or boot commands.
